newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes extend rally in Asia, light wet crudes firm.
newsitem.headline: Crudes extend rally in Asia, light wet crudes firm.

text.p: Crude oil prices gained during Asian market hours on Thursday, extending a rally started overnight. Prices were buoyed mainly by bullish weekly API stock data, traders said.

A broker attributed crude gains largely to API data, which showed draws in U.S. petroleum and refined products stocks, saying that there appeared to be little else moving the markets. The weekly API data released overnight showed that crude stocks fell by 6.6 million barrels last week, while distillate stocks declined by 827,000 barrels.
Cash December Brent was assessed at $23.90/24.00.

At 0815 GMT, December Brent was most recently traded at $24.05 on SIMEX compared with the IPE settlement of $23.89 on Wednesday. Brent's spread with Dubai was wider compared with late U.S. trading levels, mainly due to Brent's strength. The Brent/Dubai spread was notionally assessed at $2.00/2.10 for January compared with $1.92/1.97 overnight. The February Brent/Dubai spread was notionally assessed at $1.90/2.00.
The December/January Brent spread was assessed at 35/40 cents after a deal was reported done at 40 cents.
In the wet market, light Gulf crudes were well-supported by buying interest, traders said.

The market for January Murban was notionally assessed at 50 to 60 cents above the official selling price, while January Umm Shaif was notionally assessed at ADNOC plus 60 cents and Qatar Marine at QGPC plus 55-60 cents. The levels were close to or higher than last deals done for December.
In Asian crudes, some traders said China probably remained interested in December Indonesian cargoes. The requirement, however, was likely to emerge only after allocations were made.
Stasco said that it has set the term price for the sale of 1997 Oman crude to Asian customers at MPM plus 11 cents, up three cents from the 1996 premium.--M.Yoshikawa/Tokyo
